Subject: Facebook post — the shed (DRAFT, pics to go up first)

Two Saturdays ago I opened the panel on a buddy's shed and found a crime scene that was still plugged in.

I'm posting the list because it's genuinely funny, and because the punchline is "this is exactly how houses burn down."

What was actually in there:

- Power came in on three orange extension cords, daisy chained, out a basement window, across the yard, under the deck. One splice was wrapped in DUCT TAPE. Not electrical tape. Duct.
- A 30 amp breaker feeding 14 gauge wire.
- A shed outlet wired with speaker wire.
- A "GFCI" that was a regular outlet with a GFCI sticker stuck on the front. Somebody wrote a check and cashed it with a Sharpie.
- A ceiling fan box held up by ONE drywall screw. The fan weighed more than the screw did.
- A mouse nest in the junction box. The mice were fine. Unbothered. Nobody in that shed was having a worse weekend than those mice did.
- Inside the panel door, in Sharpie: SHED - DONT TOUCH - RON.

And the wife was standing right there when I opened it up and goes, "Who's Ron?" Like, how would I know, ma'am.

I'm not trying to make anybody the villain. The guy who did it wasn't evil, he was cheap and a little proud, and that's most of these. Everybody's uncle knows somebody. That's the whole problem. Everybody's uncle is one screwdriver away from a chimney fire.

So we fixed it. Trenched 18 inches, pulled 12/2 UF, real 20A GFCI breaker, real box, real outlets, and the fan got a brace instead of a prayer. Two Saturdays of work and I got paid in two pizzas and a case of Yuengling. Best money I made all year.

Now the part that isn't funny.

Every one of those items is a fire waiting on a bad day. A storm, a pinched cord, a mouse with good taste. This is the stuff that burns houses down, and here's the thing about that: it doesn't burn the guy who did the wiring. It burns the house and everybody sleeping in it.

If the person doing your electrical watched a bunch of videos, can do it for $150 cash, and tells you he doesn't pull permits because "nobody checks," he's not an electrician. He's a guy with a drill and a confident opinion.

Call a licensed guy. Not your buddy. Not the nephew. Not the guy in the comments. Licensed, insured, permit pulled and signed off, because if he's not pulling permits he's not licensed, and if he's not licensed, who's gonna answer the insurance company when they ask?

There are electricians in this town doing this for a living and they're really good at it. Pay them. It's a lot cheaper than a fire.

No names, no tags, house stays private. I'll be over here with a reciprocating saw if anybody needs a hand.
